_**Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise**_ is a 2016 science book by [psychologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychologist "Psychologist") [K. Anders Ericsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Anders_Ericsson "K. Anders Ericsson") and science writer Robert Pool. The book summarizes the findings of Ericsson's 30-year research into the general nature and acquisition of expertise.

The difference for top performers isn’t practice – it’s “deliberate practice,” a focused method of systematic improvement that psychologist Anders Ericsson spent a lifetime studying. He and co-author Robert Pool explain the science that supports deliberate practice and illustrate their manual with historical examples of top performers.

Summary

Practice and the time they devote to the practice differentiates top and average performers.

“Purposeful practice” aims at specific, well-defined targets.
Instead of practicing your golf game, think specifically about what you need to do to reduce your handicap five strokes. Focus, perhaps, on adjusting your swing.
